steps.title: Who bears most responsibility
steps.body: Those who can do the greatest harm bear the greatest responsibility to reduce danger to others.

question.prompt: Under the hierarchy of road users, the greatest responsibility lies with…

options.text: Whoever reached the road first
Pedestrians, because they're most at risk
Those whose vehicles can cause the greatest harm

question.explanation: Greater potential harm brings greater responsibility to reduce danger to others.

steps.scene: You're turning left into a side road. A pedestrian is waiting to cross the side road you're entering.

options.text: Turn quickly before they step out
Sound your horn so they wait
Give way — let them cross before you turn in

question.explanation: Give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross a road you turn into or from.

steps.title: Don't cut across
steps.body: When turning into or out of a junction or changing lane, don't cut across cyclists or horse riders going ahead.

question.prompt: A cyclist is going straight on as you wait to turn left. You should…

options.text: Wait — don't cut across their path
Accelerate to turn in ahead of them
Edge alongside them and turn slowly

question.explanation: Riders going ahead have priority — turning across them causes serious collisions.

steps.title: Passing a cyclist
steps.body: Leave at least 1.5 metres when overtaking cyclists at speeds up to 30 mph — and more space at higher speeds.

question.prompt: Overtaking a cyclist at 28 mph, leave at least…

options.text: 1.5 metres
The width of a car door
Half a metre

question.explanation: At least 1.5 m up to 30 mph; leave more room when passing faster.

steps.title: Passing horses
steps.body: Pass horse riders at under 10 mph, leaving at least 2 metres of space.

question.prompt: The safe way past a horse rider is…

options.text: Slow but close, so the horse sees you
Under 10 mph, with at least 2 metres of space
Quickly, to spend less time alongside

question.explanation: Horses spook: under 10 mph and at least 2 m of space.

steps.scene: Night, heavy rain. The cyclist ahead wobbles as gusts of wind hit them.

options.text: Nothing — cyclists must hold their line
Overtake before the next gust arrives
Give extra room — riders need more space in bad weather and at night

question.explanation: Give motorcyclists, cyclists and horse riders extra room in bad weather and at night.

steps.wrongBelief: Cars have priority over pedestrians at junctions.

options.text: Give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross a road you're turning into
It isn't wrong — bigger vehicles go first
Pedestrians only have priority at traffic lights

question.explanation: At junctions, pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross the road you turn into or from go first.

steps.repairNote: At a junction, a pedestrian crossing or waiting to cross the road you're turning into or from has priority over your car.

questions.prompt: The hierarchy of road users says…

options.text: All road users carry exactly equal responsibility
Those who can do most harm have most responsibility to reduce danger
Vulnerable users must keep out of the way

questions.explanation: The greatest capacity for harm brings the greatest responsibility.

questions.prompt: Turning into a side road where a pedestrian is crossing, you should…

options.text: Proceed — vehicles have priority
Give way to them
Pass close behind them

questions.explanation: Pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross the road you enter have priority.

questions.prompt: The minimum passing distance for a cyclist at up to 30 mph is…

options.text: Three car lengths behind them
1.5 metres
0.5 metres

questions.explanation: At least 1.5 m at up to 30 mph — more space at higher speeds.

questions.prompt: You should pass a horse rider at…

options.text: Any speed, if you give a wide berth
30 mph, about 1 metre away
Under 10 mph, at least 2 metres away

questions.explanation: Under 10 mph and at least 2 m — speed and space both matter.

questions.prompt: Before turning across a cyclist going straight ahead, you should…

options.text: Wait and avoid cutting across them
Sound your horn and complete the turn
Cut in if your vehicle is faster

questions.explanation: Don't cut across cyclists going ahead when turning into or out of a junction.
